key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, with degradation concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, including 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification to improve UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements during UV-soaking studies.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different ITO interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements identified preferential buried-interface degradation consistent with ex-situ destructive tests and showed reduced UV damage with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification.
watch_item: The abstract reports UV-soaking results without quantitative stability gains or evidence of generalization to other operational stressors.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
